title: observability: token-level + KV cache metrics, dashboard panels, and alert tuning
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: production workloads observed intermittent tail latency spikes and unexpected token-level cost regressions for bursty chat traffic. Root cause tracing showed increased KV cache miss amplification under certain batching patterns. This PR instruments token-level metrics + KV cache hit/miss breakdowns, adds a curated Grafana dashboard with drilldowns for cost/latency by route/model/region, and updates alert thresholds based on production histograms.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds token-level counters and histograms: tokens_generated, tokens_requested, token_latency_ms (per-token histogram), token_cost_units.
- Adds KV cache metrics: kv_cache_hit_count, kv_cache_miss_count, kv_cache_evictions, kv_cache_lookup_latency_ms. These are tagged by model, shard, bucket, and route.
- Emits tracing spans around KV lookups and prefix cache hits for better flamegraphing.
- Introduces a Grafana dashboard definition (token_kv_observability_dashboard.json) with panels for token cost/latency breakdown, KV hit ratio heatmap, cold-start frequency, and per-route unit cost.
- Adds alert tuning: new alerts for sustained token_latency_p95 > 1200ms for > 5m (route-level), kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.85 for 10m, and token_cost_units per-minute spike detection (anomaly rule). Alerts include runbook links and automatic rollback policies for canary rollouts.
- Updates the runbook and docs: docs/observability/runbooks/token_kv_alerts.md includes investigation steps and mitigation playbook.

Testing and rollout:
- Local unit + integration tests added under tests/observability to validate metric tags and histogram bucketing.
- End-to-end QA run on staging with synthetic workload (chat-burst profile) validated that token-level metrics correlate with the existing request traces and that KV hit ratio matches simulated expectations.
- Dashboard reviewed with SRE and Product to ensure panels surface actionable signals.
- Rollout plan: feature flag gated on telemetry.enable_token_kv_metrics and phased rollout across dedicated capacity pools over 2 days. Alerts are initially created in "warning" severity and promoted after 24h of stable signals.

Breaking changes: none. Backwards compatibility: metrics are additive and do not change existing metric names.

Notes: some telemetry enum values were extended (telemetry.proto updated) — see migration section below. Telemetry consumers (third-party dashboards) may need a quick sync to pick up the new fields.

Migration: update consumers to accept new tags (model, shard, route). The proto change is a non-breaking additive enum extension. CLI/SDKs unaffected for the API surface.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add metric emitters and tags
- [x] Instrument tracing spans
- [x] Create dashboard definition and seed dashboards in staging
- [x] Add alerts and runbook entries
- [x] Add unit/integration tests
- [x] Run staging performance validation

References: Linear ENG-4521, OBS-102; incident SUP-789 (customer-reported latency spikes).
